correctness.rationale: Color support is a surjective map from the nonempty states to the nonempty subsets of the realized colors. It preserves intersection in the forward direction and lifts any target neighbor by choosing one shared atom from the current state and representatives for its other colors. Since p_i at a state is the universal bit-i condition, atomic truth is preserved; the bounded morphism then gives invariance of every modal formula. Conversely, ◇p_i tests whether a state contains any bit-i-positive atom, via singletons. The stated δ_t tests homogeneity at t, so ◇δ_t tests local occurrence, and ◇◇δ_t tests global occurrence via the universal state followed by a singleton. This works also for the all-zero color and n=1. Thus the profile is complete, including across atom counts. Any j-color support with 1≤j≤min(n,2^k) can be assigned, repeating colors as necessary, and every nonempty subset realizes the local support. This yields the exact census and binomial stabilization. For n<m the countermodel profiles persist; if n<2^k, the explicit depth-at-most-three formula excludes simultaneous global occurrence of n+1 chosen colors and separates the stages, whereas if n≥2^k there are no further profiles. The resulting least variable count is ceil(log₂(n+1)). This uses the full frame and independent Boolean values, never arbitrary induced submodels. The bundled checker and its bounded reported cases were inspected, not executed; the proof establishes the unbounded result.

value.rationale: The full-state logic is a specified natural semantics. The classification gives a finite sufficient and necessary statistic for all fixed-alphabet modal formulas, not merely a count for a few sizes. It supplies the exact expressive cutoff and explicit short-depth witnesses for all finite-stage comparisons, distinguishing what colors can be detected within a state from those visible only globally. This goes beyond strictness with unrestrictedly many variables.
